items.title: Show HN: ReadMini – read only what matters from an article
items.contentSnippet:
HN is increasingly crowded with bloated, repetitive AI-generated articles (some examples in the first comment)
ReadMini turns an article into the version you actually need to read. It cuts what doesn’t matter, tightens what does, and reorganizes things when that makes the article clearer.
This is v0. I’d love some feedback. Billing not integrated yet.

items.title: Show HN: Web search engine built from the CommonCrawl corpus
items.contentSnippet:
Hello HN, I'm building an alternative web search engine. You can try the demo here: https://search.xorsoft.dev/
My goal was to reach 1% of Google's index. This is 4 billion pages across 33.5 million domains. I was inspired by the earlier attempts shared here: "Building a web search engine from scratch with 3B neural embeddings" [1] and "Crawling a billion web pages in just over 24 hours" [2]. items.title: Show HN: 9.8M product opinions collected from Reddit / HN, on 48,837 products
items.contentSnippet:
This is something I have been making on the side.
Opinions are extracted from posts and comments using a 8x 3090 box I had spare, using Gemma models, then summaries are created from the opinions. Several methods are used to exclude spam / shills.
You can also browse by recommendations from a specific subreddit.
The map view on the travel category is pretty neat: https://www.trustmebro.reviews/c/travel?view=map

items.title: Show HN: Cross Origin Tracking Safari
items.contentSnippet:
So this is a proof of concept to demonstrate how cross origin tracking could work in Safari. Turn consent into a captcha once and silently track the user going forward. Upsides: this could let you complete a captcha on one site, and have its grant carry over to another site seamlessly.
Downsides: Cross origin tracking.
